functions.name: HookPayload::parse_json
functions.behavior: Ports the inline python in agent-hook.sh (lines 21-32) that decodes the agent's hook JSON on stdin into the fields the protocol needs. Reads dual-cased keys, preferring snake_case then camelCase: transcript = transcript_path || transcriptPath || ""; session_id = session_id || sessionId || ""; cwd = cwd (default ""); recoverable = the JSON bool `recoverable`; and stamps an attention_token = current monotonic time in nanoseconds (time.time_ns()). Returns a HookPayload{session_id, cwd, transcript, recoverable: Option<bool>, token: u128}. This is the inbound hook->daemon message decoder.
functions.side_effects: Reads the wall/monotonic clock to mint the token (time.time_ns()). No filesystem.
edge_cases: Invalid or empty JSON: the python is wrapped in `2>/dev/null || true`, so a decode failure yields an all-empty `parsed` block; downstream, empty session_id (line 36) causes the whole hook to exit 0 silently. Rust must mirror: a parse error is not fatal, it degrades to an empty payload that the caller treats as a no-op.

recoverable tri-state: python prints "true"/"false"/"" for True/False/absent. Must be Option<bool> (None when the key is missing or not a JSON bool), NOT defaulted to false, because only copilot+recoverable==Some(true) reroutes an error event.
session_id containing '/' is sanitized to '_' by the shell AFTER parse (line 35: `${session_id//\//_}`); replace ALL slashes, not just the first. This sanitized id is what forms filenames/keys.

cwd default: python defaults cwd to ""; the shell later substitutes $PWD when empty at record-write time (line 85 `${cwd:-$PWD}`), not here. Keep the empty-string here and apply the PWD fallback in the record serializer / daemon, matching where the shell does it.
transcript may be absent (turn events without a payload path) -> empty string, which suppresses refresh_record (agent-hook.sh line 98).

time_ns granularity: two events in the same session within one clock tick could collide; the token is only required monotonic-nondecreasing per session for the claim logic (<= is rejected). Use a nanosecond clock; do not truncate to millis.

functions.name: normalize_event
functions.signature: pub fn normalize_event(agent: &str, raw_event: &str, recoverable: Option<bool>) -> EventKind
functions.behavior: Ports agent-hook.sh lines 39-45. Maps the CLI event arg (start|end|working|needsAttention|error, default start) plus agent+recoverable into the canonical EventKind{Start, End, Working, NeedsAttention}. An `error` event becomes Working when agent=="copilot" AND recoverable==Some(true) (a recoverable Copilot error keeps the session working), otherwise becomes NeedsAttention. All other events pass through unchanged.
edge_cases: Only `error` is remapped; `start`/`working`/`needsAttention`/`end` pass through verbatim.

recoverable is compared to the literal string "true" in bash (from the python "true"/"false"/""); in Rust compare recoverable==Some(true). A recoverable error from a non-copilot agent still becomes NeedsAttention (the agent guard is ANDed).
Default event when arg omitted is `start` (line 18 `${2:-start}`).
Any unrecognized event string is treated by the shell's final fallthrough (line 162) as start/register; preserve that: unknown -> Start-equivalent (re)register.

functions.name: RegistryRecord::serialize
functions.behavior: Ports register_session's printf (agent-hook.sh line 85) and refresh_record's printf (lines 112-114). Emits exactly five TAB-separated fields terminated by one '\n': pane\tagent\tpid\tcwd\ttranscript. pane is the empty string for a daemon/pane-less session (no TMUX_PANE). cwd falls back to PWD (register) or the old cwd (refresh) when the event's cwd is empty. pid is the empty string when the ancestry walk found no agent process.
functions.side_effects: None itself; the daemon writes the returned bytes to sessions/<agent>-<session_id> (mkdir -p first).
edge_cases: ALWAYS five fields even when pane and/or pid are empty; empty fields are preserved as adjacent tabs, never collapsed. A leading empty pane field (pane-less session) MUST be written as a bare leading tab.
Exactly one trailing newline; the reader rstrips only '\n'.
cwd fallback ordering: register uses ${cwd:-$PWD}; refresh uses ${cwd:-$old_cwd}. These are two different fallbacks for the same slot - keep them distinct.
The record filename/key is <agent>-<session_id> (line 85), not the raw session_id; the daemon store is keyed by that composite.

functions.name: RegistryRecord::parse
functions.behavior: Ports sidebar.py fetch_agent_sessions parsing (lines 427-437). Reads a record's bytes, rstrips ONLY the trailing '\n', splits on '\t' preserving empty fields. Field-count dispatch: len==2 is the legacy claude-hook.sh format (pane, cwd) synthesized as {pane, agent:"claude", pid:"", cwd, transcript:""}; len>=4 is the current format (pane, agent, pid, cwd, transcript?) where transcript is fields[4] or "" when only 4 fields; any other length (0,1,3) returns None (record skipped, not pruned).
functions.side_effects: None (pure over the already-read bytes). The read itself is a separate IO step; an OSError on read means `continue` (skip), distinct from a parse-length skip.
edge_cases: MUST rstrip('\n') not trim/strip: a pane-less record starts with a tab, and trimming whitespace would eat the empty leading pane field and shift every field left (agent-hook.sh's refresh_record comment lines 100-103, and sidebar comment lines 424-426 spell this out). This is the single most important framing quirk.
Legacy 2-field back-compat is mandatory (CLAUDE.md Conventions): pane<TAB>cwd, agent forced to "claude", empty pid (which then means 'trusted, no pid to verify').
len==3 is intentionally rejected (falls through the elif to `else: continue`).

len>=5 keeps only fields 0..4; any extra tab-fields (e.g. a tab in a path/title) are dropped - a path is deemed unlikely to contain a tab (sidebar comment lines 271-275). Preserve the >=5 truncation, do not error.

Empty pid string is significant: pid.isdigit()==false marks a legacy/unverified record that is TRUSTED (occupies its recorded pane without an ancestry check) - see assoc. Do not coerce empty pid to 0.

functions.name: parse_field_int
functions.behavior: The shared 'digit-string or nothing' primitive used everywhere the protocol stores an integer as text: pid (pid.isdigit()), attention/notified token (token.isdigit()), width (value.isdigit()), pane_pid, pb_progress. Returns Some(n) only when the string is a non-empty run of ASCII decimal digits, else None.
edge_cases: Parity with Python str.isdigit(): must return None for the empty string, for any string containing a sign ('-'/'+'), whitespace, or a decimal point, and for a leading/trailing-space number. Do NOT use Rust's str::parse which accepts leading '+' and surrounding behavior differs; gate on chars().all(is_ascii_digit) && !is_empty first.

Python str.isdigit() also returns true for some Unicode digit/superscript codepoints; the values here are ASCII-only in practice (pids, ns tokens, tmux numbers), so ASCII-digit gating is the correct and safer port. Note this as a deliberate narrowing, not an accidental divergence.
Width and token are large (ns tokens exceed u64 range over long uptimes? no - ns since epoch fits u64 until year 2262, but use u128 to be safe for token math and comparisons).

functions.name: attention_marker_read
functions.behavior: Ports _attention_token (sidebar.py lines 354-363). Opens the attention marker, strips it, and if the content is a digit-string returns that int token; if the file exists but is empty/non-digit (a legacy marker written before tokens) returns the file's st_mtime_ns as the token; any OSError (missing file) returns None. None means 'no attention'.
functions.side_effects: Reads the file and, on the legacy path, stat()s it for mtime_ns.
edge_cases: Legacy empty-marker fallback to mtime_ns is required back-compat; a marker touched by an old hook still yields a stable, comparable token.

Here .strip() (full strip) IS used on the token content (line 358) - unlike the record, this single-value field has no empty-preservation concern. Keep strip() here but rstrip('\n') for records; they differ deliberately.
Missing file -> None (not an error). This is the common case and gates the whole 'attention' status.
mtime_ns must be nanoseconds to be comparable with the ns tokens written by the current hook; do not downgrade to seconds.

functions.name: attention_marker_write
functions.signature: pub fn write_attention_marker(path: &Path, token: AttnToken) -> io::Result<()>
functions.behavior: Ports agent-hook.sh line 156 (`printf '%s\n' "$attention_token" > marker`). Writes the decimal token plus a newline, truncating. Part of the needsAttention branch which also mkdir -p's ATTENTION and rm's the working marker (mutual exclusion).
functions.side_effects: Writes the attention marker; the caller must also delete the working marker to preserve mutual exclusion.
edge_cases: Must be paired with removal of the working marker (line 157) - the two turn-state markers are mutually exclusive (CLAUDE.md invariant); writing one without clearing the other corrupts turn state.
One trailing newline (the reader strips it anyway, but match the format).
Token is the payload's minted ns token, not a fresh clock read at write time - the same token travels from parse to marker so the client's claim dedup matches.

functions.name: working_marker
functions.signature: pub fn write_working_marker(path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> / pub fn working_marker_exists(path: &Path) -> bool
functions.behavior: Ports the working branch (agent-hook.sh lines 145-147) and the client's existence test (sidebar.py line 494, 538). The working marker is a zero-byte file whose mere existence is the flag (`: > marker`). The client reads status as 'working' only when the attention token is None AND the working marker exists.
functions.side_effects: write: creates/truncates an empty file (mkdir -p WORKING first) and the caller rm's the attention marker (mutual exclusion). exists: stat only.
edge_cases: Content is irrelevant - existence only. Do not read/parse it.

Attention strictly wins over working in the client's status resolution (line 493-494): if an attention token is present, status is 'attention' regardless of the working marker. Preserve this precedence.
end event removes both markers and the record (line 132).

functions.name: claim_attention
functions.signature: pub fn claim_attention(dir: &Path, key: &str, token: AttnToken) -> bool
functions.behavior: Ports _claim_attention (sidebar.py lines 585-605). The cross-process single-fire dedup for bell/notification. Opens notified/<key> with append+read, takes an exclusive flock, reads the previous token, and claims (returns true) iff token > previous_token, writing the new token back under the lock; otherwise returns false. This is the coordination message between the many per-window client instances (or, in the new design, the arbitration the daemon performs).
functions.side_effects: Creates NOTIFIED dir; creates/opens the flag file; holds an advisory exclusive lock (fcntl LOCK_EX) for the read-compare-write; truncates and rewrites the flag on a successful claim.
edge_cases: previous_token resolution has THREE cases: digit content -> int; non-digit content but file pre-existed -> the flag file's OWN st_mtime_ns (fstat, line 596) so legacy empty flags don't let every poll reclaim; file did not pre-exist -> 0.
Strict '>' semantics: token <= previous_token returns false (line 597). Equal tokens do NOT re-fire. This is what makes exactly one window's instance win each event.

The lock must cover the entire read-compare-write; without atomicity two instances could both claim. In the new daemon design a single owner may replace flock with an in-process mutex, but the token-monotonic + strict-'>' rule must survive.
Any OSError returns false (do not fire) - failing closed avoids duplicate signals.
Key is the composite <agent>-<session_id> (same filename as the registry record), not the bare session id.

functions.name: prune_notified_flags
functions.signature: pub fn prune_notified_flags(notified_dir: &Path, registry_dir: &Path, now: SystemTime)
functions.behavior: Ports the tail of notify_attention (sidebar.py lines 652-668). Retains a session's notified flag while its registry record exists; a flag whose record is gone is deleted only after its mtime is >= 5 seconds old, a grace longer than any in-flight poll so a stale poll can't reclaim an older event after focus cleared the marker.
functions.side_effects: Lists NOTIFIED, stats each flag, unlinks expired ones.
edge_cases: Keep-alive is by presence of REGISTRY/<name> (same key); only orphaned flags are eligible for deletion.
The 5-second grace is load-bearing (must exceed the poll cadence); keep the constant and the '>=' comparison.
OSError on list -> empty; per-flag OSError -> skip. Best-effort.

functions.name: record_key / split_key
functions.signature: pub fn record_key(agent: &str, session_id: &str) -> String  /  pub fn session_id_from_key(key: &str, agent: &str) -> &str
functions.behavior: The composite-key framing used for every per-session file (sessions/, attention/, working/, notified/). Ports line 85 (`$agent-$session_id`) and sidebar.py lines 449-450 (`prefix = agent + "-"; session_id = name[len(prefix):] if name.startswith(prefix) else name`). record_key joins agent and sanitized session_id with a single '-'; session_id_from_key strips the leading '<agent>-' prefix if present, else returns the whole name.
edge_cases: session_id must already be slash-sanitized ('/'->'_') before keying (hook line 35).
Prefix strip is conditional: if the name does not start with '<agent>-' (shouldn't happen but defensive), return the name unchanged - do not panic on a missing prefix.
The bare stripped session_id is used ONLY to look up labels/titles (session_meta); the composite key remains the session's identity everywhere else (status, claim, selection). Don't conflate the two.

functions.name: selection read/write
functions.signature: pub fn read_selection(path: &Path) -> Option<Vec<String>>  /  pub fn write_selection(path: &Path, key: &[String])
functions.behavior: Ports read_selection/write_selection (sidebar.py lines 545-560), the shared-highlight message. write joins the key components with '\t' (no trailing newline). read rstrips '\n', splits on '\t', and returns None if the result is empty or its first element is empty (falsy), else the tuple. An agent row's key is ("a", session_id, pane); window/pane keys have other shapes - proto only frames the tuple, the shapes belong to rows.
functions.side_effects: write: mkdir -p STATE_DIR then overwrite the file. read: one read.
edge_cases: rstrip('\n') again (not full strip) - though selection components are unlikely to have leading tabs, match the record discipline for consistency.
Empty file or empty-first-component -> None (line 551 `parts and parts[0]`).
Variable arity: 3-tuple for agents, different for windows/panes; parse as Vec<String>, don't fix the length.
This is arguably owned by the rows/client module; proto supplies the tab-join/tab-split framing. Listed here because it shares the framing invariants; final home can be rows if preferred.

side_effects: Filesystem: reads/writes the per-session record files (sessions/), the mutually-exclusive turn markers (working/, attention/), the flock-guarded notified/ flags, and the shared selection file, all under $XDG_STATE_HOME/tmux-agent-wrangler (default ~/.local/state). Holds an advisory fcntl exclusive lock during claim_attention. Mints nanosecond tokens from the clock. Pure sub-layer: the serialize/parse/normalize/field-int helpers have no side effects and should be split out so they are unit-testable without a filesystem.
parity_risks: rstrip('\n') vs strip(): records AND selection strip ONLY the trailing newline to preserve an empty leading field (pane-less/daemon records begin with a tab); the single-value token marker uses full strip(). Getting this wrong shifts every record field left and the client prunes the record as a bogus non-local pane (agent-hook.sh lines 100-103, sidebar.py lines 424-426).

Python str.isdigit() semantics: the empty string, signed numbers, and whitespace-padded numbers are all non-digit; empty pid specifically means 'legacy/unverified, trust it' rather than 0. Rust must gate on non-empty ASCII-digit runs, not str::parse (which accepts '+'), and must not coerce empty pid to 0.

Attention token is a monotonic ns value with a legacy fallback to the marker's st_mtime_ns; the notified-flag previous_token has a THREE-way resolution (digit / pre-existing-file-mtime_ns / 0). Downgrading any of these to seconds, or dropping the mtime fallback, breaks dedup against markers/flags written by the old hook.

Strict '>' in claim_attention: equal tokens must NOT re-fire; '<=' returns false. This single comparison is what makes exactly one of the N per-window instances signal each event. An off-by-one to '>=' causes duplicate bells/notifications.

Mutual-exclusion invariant of the two turn markers: writing working MUST delete attention and vice-versa; end deletes record+working+attention. The proto layer that writes one marker must also clear the other, or the client shows a stale state (attention always wins in status resolution, masking a live 'working').

Legacy 2-field record back-compat (pane<TAB>cwd -> agent 'claude', empty pid) is a hard requirement (CLAUDE.md); a 3-field record is intentionally rejected (skip, not prune); >=5 fields are truncated to 5 (a tab inside a path/title is assumed absent). Field-count dispatch must match exactly.

Composite key <agent>-<session_id> is the identity for record/marker/notified/selection files; the bare prefix-stripped session_id is used ONLY for label lookup. Conflating them mis-keys the claim/marker files.
session_id slash sanitization ('/'->'_', ALL occurrences) happens in the hook before keying; if the daemon re-derives keys it must apply the same substitution or records won't line up.
cwd fallback differs by path: register substitutes $PWD for an empty cwd, refresh substitutes the old record's cwd. Two different defaults for the same slot.
5-second notified-flag grace must exceed the poll/relayout cadence; shortening it lets a stale in-flight poll reclaim an already-signalled older event.

Record listing order (sorted(os.listdir)) is lexicographic and feeds downstream title-collision tie-breaking determinism (assoc); a HashMap/undefined iteration order in Rust would make ambiguous placements nondeterministic. Sort keys lexicographically by byte/str.

recoverable is tri-state (Some(true)/Some(false)/None); only copilot+Some(true) reroutes an error to Working. Defaulting None to false changes non-copilot and missing-field behavior only subtly, but defaulting to true would wrongly suppress attention.

JSON parse failure is non-fatal and degrades to an empty payload (=> silent no-op / exit 0), not an error; the daemon must swallow malformed hook input the way the `2>/dev/null || true` shell wrapper does.
